html:
In the night of 10 to 11 September 2023, Storm Daniel brought torrential rain to eastern Libya and burst two dams above the coastal city of Derna. A flood wave swept down the valley through the city centre, carrying whole buildings and people into the sea. Thousands died; counts range from about 4,000 to well over 10,000, with many still missing.

Storm Daniel was a rare Mediterranean storm with tropical features, a "medicane", that had already flooded Greece.

The two earth dams, Abu Mansour and Derna, were built in the 1970s by a Yugoslav firm. Engineers had warned for years that they needed repair. Libya had been split between rival governments since the fall of Gaddafi in the Arab Spring, and money set aside for maintenance was never spent. Officials told residents to stay home on the night of the storm.

The disaster set off protests in Derna, and officials were later tried for neglect. It is one of the deadliest dam failures since the Banqiao Dam collapse in China in 1975.
